module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 115

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/115](https://www.erdosproblems.com/115)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [ErLe94] Erëmenko, A. and Lempert, L., *An extremal problem for polynomials*. Proc. Amer. Math.
  Soc. (1994), 191-193.
- [Po59a] Pommerenke, Ch., *On the derivative of a polynomial*. Michigan Math. J. (1959), 373-375.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos115

/--
If $p(z)$ is a polynomial of degree $n$ such that $\{z : \lvert p(z)\rvert\leq 1\}$ is connected
then is it true that
$$\max_{\substack{z\in\mathbb{C}\\ \lvert p(z)\rvert\leq 1}} \lvert p'(z)\rvert
\leq (\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))n^2?$$

Eremenko and Lempert [ErLe94] have shown this is true, and in fact Chebyshev polynomials are the
extreme examples.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos115.lean"]
theorem erdos_115 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ p : Polynomial ℂ, p.Monic → p.natDegree = n →
      IsConnected {z : ℂ | ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1} → ∀ z : ℂ, ‖p.eval z‖ ≤ 1 →
        ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ ≤ (1 / 2 + ε) * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos115

findings.description: The docstring at lines 41–44 omits “monic,” although the Lean statement correctly requires `p.Monic`. This normalization is mathematically necessary: for every positive n, pₙ(z) = (nz)^n has connected unit lemniscate {|z| ≤ 1/n} and |pₙ′(1/n)| = n², contradicting the unnormalized asymptotic bound. The formal proposition itself is faithful to the primary sources; only its prose needs correction. The counterexample to the complete unnormalized asymptotic statement was proved in Lean in the scratch file.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős [Er61], §IV.1, pp.246–247, begins with a polynomial z^n + … before posing the derivative question (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1961-22.pdf). Eremenko–Lempert [ErLe94], abstract, p.191, explicitly assume f(z) = z^n + … and prove max_E |f′| ≤ 2^(1/n−1)n² (https://www.math.purdue.edu/~eremenko/dvi/lempert.pdf). The brief statement on erdosproblems.com also omits the normalization, but these primary references specify it.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring’s opening to “If p(z) is a monic polynomial of degree n …”. Retain the existing `p.Monic` hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: The Lean conclusion bounds the derivative at every point of the unit lemniscate instead of explicitly bounding its maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive degree, the unit lemniscate of a complex polynomial is compact, and for a monic polynomial it is nonempty. The derivative norm is continuous, so its maximum is attained. Consequently the pointwise upper bound is equivalent to the same bound on that maximum. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. Degree zero does not affect the eventual statement; its only monic polynomial is 1, whose derivative is zero.

review.notes: No defect was found in the Lean proposition. Its uniform epsilon/eventual quantifiers correctly express the asymptotic bound, and a kernel-checked scratch lemma derives it from the published sharp bound. Boundary cases, nonemptiness, and satisfiability in every positive degree were checked. The source currently records an affirmative solution verified in Lean, consistent with the file’s metadata. The linked proof states the stronger sharp bound and contains no explicit sorry/admit or custom axioms; recompilation under the sandbox’s v4.33.1 encounters compatibility errors, whereas the linked file targets v4.29.1, so its native-version proof was not independently revalidated. Full texts of [Er90] and [Po59a] could not be accessed; their relevant claims are discussed explicitly in the accessible [ErLe94] paper.
